title: World Bank: AI eased homework but lowered China exam scores
key_facts: The World Bank's World Development Report 2026 has a section on generative AI and the erosion of learning and skills.
Its strongest evidence is a study of Chinese students in classes 7 to 12: self-reported AI use rose from almost zero to about 80% between 2022 and 2025.
Six months after first use, homework scores rose 18% while monthly in-class exam scores fell 20%.
Students who had ever used AI scored 5-7% lower on average in senior high-school and college entrance exams.
The report says the study is not yet peer-reviewed and reflects an early phase of AI adoption.
Experiments in several countries found 30 sessions of AI tutoring gave learning gains of at least about half a year of schooling when it complemented teachers.
quote_evidence: Six months after its first use, homework scores improved 18% even as students spent less time on assignments, while monthly in-class examination scores fell 20%.
The report cautioned that the study had not yet been peer-reviewed and reflected the early phase of AI adoption.
why_it_matters_hint: Evidence that unrestricted AI use can raise homework results while lowering real learning.
event_date: report published October 2026 (exact date not stated)
